spec_match.rationale: The three decode probes exercise the real support surface (img natural size, createImageBitmap, canvas pixel readback) against a genuine served image/jxl file, and the page correctly teaches that only a decode is proof.

interactive.rationale: Auto-runs on load with a Run-again button; each probe row shows live result plus what it proves, and the side-by-side jxl/png comparison is real content.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Both this page's lede and the feature index promise the fourth probe is 'the Accept header the browser sends', but the implemented probe reads the server's response Content-Type via HEAD — the request Accept header is never read or displayed.

edge_cases.rationale: The non-decoding browser is the exercised case here: all three decode probes fail with named errors while the Content-Type row stays yes, and the narration explains exactly why that disagreement makes header checks a bad support probe.

conformance.rationale: Most of the feature suite is real behavioural probing (dimensions, pixel variance, decode-only boundary), but its picture-negotiation-skips-undecodable-types assertion contains a try block with no catch/finally and can never execute in any browser — flagged below for a human.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: verdict 'This browser does not decode JPEG XL'; rows read no/0x0-style failures ('InvalidStateError: The source image could not be decoded') for the three decode probes and yes for Content-Type: image/jxl; Run again re-populated all four rows; the only failed requests were the expected aborted .jxl loads; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each run logs per-probe results and emits showcaseTelemetry.assert('jxl-probed', …) with the decode count and verdict.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, verdict banner recolours border and text together, ok/bad cells combine colour with text, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Captioned table with scoped headers, images carry descriptive alt text, the verdict is text not just colour, and the narration is an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; preview figures stack on mobile with legible captions.

openQuestions.title: Actually surface the request Accept header, or reword probe four
openQuestions.detail: The lede and the feature-index card both sell the fourth probe as 'the Accept header the browser sends', but a page cannot read its own request headers — the implemented probe reports the response Content-Type instead, and its table row honestly says so. Either add a small echo route under the feature folder (per the HTTP-feature rule in CLAUDE.md invariant 7 — server.ts is routine-fenced, so queue it as a manual task) that returns the received Accept header for an image request, making the negotiation-vs-decode disagreement fully demonstrable, or fix the copy in both places to say Content-Type.

openQuestions.title: Flag: conformance assertion picture-negotiation-skips-undecodable-types is unrunnable
openQuestions.detail: FOR A HUMAN, per the immutable-conformance rule — not edited by this review. In v155/jpeg-xl-decoding-support-image-jxl-in-blink/conformance.json the assertion's test is an async IIFE opening try{ with no catch or finally; the /conformance/ runner reports 'Missing catch or finally after try' (verified on the live route, where it is the only failure that is a SyntaxError rather than a missing decoder). It can therefore never pass in any browser, including Chrome 155, even though the behaviour it describes (typed <picture> fall-through) is true and was verified live on the picture-fallback page. A human should repair the expression.

summary: A genuinely instructive probe page whose interesting state — decoders absent, labelling correct — is exactly what Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) provides: verified over CDP at http://localhost:3000/v155/jpeg-xl-decoding-support-image-jxl-in-blink/decode-probe/ with all three decode probes failing diagnosably, the Content-Type row passing, honest narration, clean console, and no overflow on either device class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 3 pass / 4 fail; three failures are honest missing-decoder results, but the fourth (picture-negotiation) is a syntactically broken assertion that can never run — flagged for a human. The 'Accept header' copy oversells what the fourth probe reads.
